race_formats.format: Heats lined up by driver's 3-event IMCA point average, inverted (lowest avg to front); B-features transfer; up to 24+ starters in A. Track may run 1 draw/redraw night per 4 points nights (2026).

race_formats.body: DIRTcar World Short Track Championship (Charlotte dirt, 2021)
race_formats.format: Pro (crate) Late Model: Thursday 20-lap feature (top 10 qualifiers + track champions + provisionals, full redraw); Saturday 30-lap feature, 26 cars incl. 4 provisionals (2 DIRTcar Pro LM points, 2 Crate Racin USA points) plus pre-entry provisionals; Last Chance Showdown pays $200-250. 6 tires total for event; 4 marked for qualifying/heats/B-mains. $100 entry; $20 temporary membership.

Pill draw sets heat start; heats lined heads-up from draw. Passing points: finish points 59 for heat win, -4 per position, plus 1.76 pts per spot gained (-0.01 per spot lost, tiebreak only). Feature lined straight up by total passing points across all heats, no invert. Consi finishes heads-up for transfers; no passing points in consi/feature. Tail starters forfeit passing points.

race_formats.body: Lucas Oil Late Model Dirt Series (2024)
race_formats.format: Hot laps (1 session); time trials 2 laps each in pill-draw order (heads-up <=27 cars, Group A/B for 28+); time trials set heat lineups (invert announced at drivers meeting). 8-lap heats: <=27 cars 3 heats top 6 transfer; <=48 cars 4 heats top 4; 49+ 6 heats top 3. 10-lap B-mains (split if >16 cars). Up to 2 points provisionals (perfect attendance) then fast-time provisional, plus promoter's option. Same 4 tires for time trials and heats. Entry fee $125/event (waived for perfect attendance). Lucky dog until 10 to go (50+ lap features) or 5 to go; double-file restarts.

Opening night draw/redraw; afterwards heats lined by 3-race point average stagger-inverted (lowest avg front). Heats/invert by car count: <=10 cars 1 heat invert 10; 11-18 2 heats invert 6 each (12); 19-24 3 heats invert 4 (12); 25-35 4 heats invert 3 (12). Invert qualifiers lined by point average; must finish on lead lap to make invert. B-features straight up. Laps: heats 6 (5 for Compact/Crown Vic); A-feature Modified 18, Stock Car/SportMod/Hobby 15 (16 if 20+ cars), Compact 12, Crown Vic 10. Missing a night loses your point average.

Heats by pill draw; feature and consi lineups by passing points. Two-spin rule (one-spin for Sport Mods). One track provisional per season, only for drivers who attempted every event incl. non-points races; touring-type classes (Super LM, Steel Block LM, Sprints, Sport Compact) get no provisionals. Year-end awards require attempting 75% of events.

Opening night: draw for heats, qualifiers redraw for feature (1 heat redraw 5; 2 or 5 heats redraw 10; 3/4/6 heats redraw 12). After: heats lined by 3-event IMCA point average, stagger-inverted (lowest avg to front); feature top 5/10/12 qualifiers inverted by point average depending on number of heats; remaining lined straight up from heats/B. B-mains lined straight up from heats. Late Models need 3 heats at 18+ cars. One draw/redraw night allowed per 4 point nights. No double features except rainouts.

IMCA classes use IMCA lineup procedure (point-average stagger invert). Non-IMCA nights: computer random draw (1-100 via MyRacePass) sets heats, max 10 cars/heat; heats 6-8 laps; semi 10-12 laps (8-10 for MLM/Mini Stock); feature redraw of top 3 (2 heats) or top 2 (3-4 heats); 16 transfer with 2 or 4 heats, 15 with 3; features up to 20 cars, no provisionals. Features: Modified/SportMod 25 laps (30 min), Stock Car/Hobby 20 laps (25 min), Mini Stock/MLM/Valley Sportsman 15 laps (20 min). Heat races 1 min/lap time limit, one-and-done caution rule. Transponder rental $20/night.

Pill-draw heats with passing points: +5 per position gained, -1.5 per position lost, plus finish points (5th to 1st = 120; 1st to 5th = 66). Top 24 in passing points go to that night's qualifying feature, top 6 redraw, 7-24 straight up. Last-chance races from top 16 weekend passing points not yet qualified. Top 8 in a qualifying feature can lock into Saturday championship feature or forfeit to try again.

race_formats.body: 141 Speedway King of the Creek (IMCA Stock Car, 2025)

All events lined up by time trials ('we will qualify for a position in all events'); features 75 laps when 10+ cars; caution laps do not count; 5 warm-up laps; transponder rental form at registration.

Practice (early practice $100/car), time trials on new impounded Hoosier F-45 stickers (max 4 for race), 150-lap one-segment feature with caution laps counted, possible fuel stop, lucky dog; must buy 20 gallons Sunoco 110 at track. $100 inspection/entry fee ($150 late).

Single-lap time trials (two laps at officials' discretion) set the field; ties broken by track points; rainout -> lineup by points or draw. Caution laps do not count in races under 100 laps. $25 extra entry per additional division. Reserved pit space $100/season. Point fund requires running 90% of events and top 5 attending banquet.
Tire-bank weekly format: tires from a season bank; new competitors on 4 new tires start rear; qualifying sets heat/feature order with inversion based on tires declared.

race_formats.body: Wisconsin International Raceway Quarter Mile Late Model Series
race_formats.format: Group practice/scuff, group qualifying, then twin 15-lap features. Feature 1: invert up to 12 qualifiers by qualifying order; cars >0.5 s off fast time start at rear. Feature 2: top half of feature 1 inverted to the rear, bottom half to the front by qualifying time; no car on front row in both. GM 602 crate engines.

Qualifying (2 flights at 42+ cars) + heats (6 heats at 42+, top 3 transfer); top 6 in qual+heat points to Dash, invert 0/4/6 by dice; A-Main first 3 rows from Dash; B-Main transfers 4-6 by car count; 2 provisionals
Wednesday-Saturday; ~100 cars; two preliminary qualifying nights with passing-point/qualifying points; Saturday 50-lap A-main (extended to 50 in 2010).

Pill draw for hot laps and time-trial order; qualifying sets heat lineups only, invert 4 in heats. 2 heats up to 17 cars, 3 heats 18-27, 4 heats 28-36. Features: Sprint/Late Model 25 laps or 30 min; Modified 20 laps/25 min; Super Stock 15 laps, Mini Stock 12 laps (20 min).

Pill draw sets heat lineups (heads-up). Feature lined by heat finish, with previous week's top 3 placed behind all heat qualifiers; drivers absent the prior event start behind them; non-qualifiers at the rear. Transponders mandatory (rental available); Raceceivers $99.95 or $15/race rental.

Three segments of 100, 100 and 200 laps, each paying $25,000 to the winner and full PASS points to the field; overall purse ($25k to win, $1,500 to start) paid by lowest combined segment finishes.
2025: SLM qualifying (two laps), 50-lap Last Chance Race transferring 4 (or two 25-lap LCQs if 30+ cars), 300-lap Snowball Derby; PLM Snowflake 125 same weekend.

history.fact: Weekly feature to-win ~$500-600 in the 1970s-80s vs ~$1,000-1,200 for crate late models in 2018.
NASCAR Winston Racing Series 1982-2000; Dodge Weekly Series 2001-2006; Whelen All-American Series 2007-2019; Advance Auto Parts Weekly Series 2020-2025; NASCAR Local Racing Series (O'Reilly) 2026-.
Restrictor plates mandated at Daytona and Talladega after 1987; used through 2019 (tapered spacer 'superspeedway' package after).
IMCA engine claim was $325 (1989); still $325 in 1997 Wisconsin IMCA Modified rules.
Competitive big-block modified engine ~$20,000 c.1993 vs $50-60,000 c.2013.
Hoosier vs Goodyear tire war in Cup in 1994; Goodyear sole supplier afterwards.
Mid-1990s major DLM races paid ~$10,000 to win; still ~$10,000 typical in 2019 while engine costs reached ~$50,000.
Mid-1990s LMSC season ~$50-60k with ~$100 tires and $10-15k engines; by 2018 ~$150-200k per season and ~$200 tires (Dale Earnhardt Jr.).
1995 to-win: World 100 $28k (2025: $72k); Knoxville Nationals $100k of $501k (2024: $190k of $1.15M). Snowball Derby ~$20-25k for decades until $30k 2022, $50k 2024.

Hooters Cup late models (1995) -> Hooters Pro Cup steel-bodied cars from 1997 (USAR Pro Cup); North/South divisions 2001-2014 with Five Champions Challenge playoff; Hooters sponsorship ended 2009; became CARS Tour 2015 with Late Model Stock + Super Late Model; Pro Late Model replaced SLM 2022; bought by Earnhardt/Burton/Harvick/Trackhouse Jan 2023 (zMAX sponsor).
Indiana weekly sprint to-win went from $600-800 to $800-1,000 in the late 1990s; weekly local to-win amounts have grown far less than special-event purses since.
SKUSA SuperNationals created (SKUSA founded 1994); gearbox classes only until 2004.
IRL launches 4.0L NA production-based engines ($75k) and capped chassis ($263k) vs CART leases ~$1.4-2M/season.
Rotax 125 MAX TaG engine reaches market (1997/98) and rapidly gains share as sealed, low-cost single-speed class.
Spec Miata approved as SCCA Southwest Division regional class; first race July 24, 1999.
Pro All Stars Series founded 2001 (first race Lee USA, May 20, 2001); PASS South 2006-2018; Oxford 250 became PASS points race from 2013 after Tom Mayberry bought Oxford Plains (late 2012).
Indy Lights (IRL) switches to Dallara IPS + Infiniti 3.5L V8 420 hp (2002-2014).

history.topic: GM circle-track sealed crate engines introduced
history.fact: GM Racing/GM Performance Parts developed circle-track crate packages in 2001 and released the 88958602, 88958603 and 88958604 sealed crate engines in 2002; they spread through limited/crate late model, street stock and modified classes over the 2000s.
GM Performance Parts introduced sealed circle-track crate engines (602/603/604) in 2002 after 2001 development; 602 first aimed at a Mid-East 602 Late Model class.
Common body templates introduced for Cup.
Mazdaspeed Miata Cup begins (national MX-5 Cup 2006; ND car 2016; IMSA sanction 2021; Michelin tires 2024).
NeSmith Chevrolet crate late model series launched 2004 (604 w/ 602 at +100 lb break); critics said crates would never work; CT525 tour planned 2013.
TaG (single-speed) classes debut at SuperNationals.
Chase for the Nextel Cup introduced: top 10 after 26 races eligible; win points raised 175 -> 180.
Hoosier became IMCA tire partner after testing at Boone in 2005; by 2015 G60-15 (Mod/Stock/N.SportMod), Chain Link (LM), RaceSaver (sprints), '500' (S.SportMod); deal extended through 2020.
CPI formula (win %, top-5 %, car counts, starts) used 1982-2004 replaced in 2005 by position points (2 per position, 25-car cap) with field-size bonus and divisional (I-V) format.
Claim raised to about $525 in mid-2000s, then settled at $500 + $50 fees ($550) for Hobby/SportMod/Stock Car, still $550 in 2026.
Toyota entered USAC National Midget competition in 2006 (20th year in 2025).
CoT part-time 2007, full-time 2008 (pulled forward as cost saving); one car type for all tracks.
WISSOTA show points capped at 12 (16+ cars) in 2007, max night 57; by 2026 a 13-point tier for 26+ cars makes max 58.
SRO GT4 class first raced 2007 as cheaper alternative to GT3.
Win points raised to 185 (15-pt gap to 2nd).
Nov 2008: testing at NASCAR-sanctioned tracks banned in top three series as a cost cut.
Rear wing replaced by spoiler in 2010.
World of Outlaws sprint cars required Goodyear rear tires from the Feb 2010 Florida DIRTcar Nationals.
Field cap for national points cut to 20 cars (40 pts to win), 5-pt win bonus.
USF2000 relaunched with Mazda MZR 2.0 and Van Diemen DP08; Cooper spec tire 2010-2023.
One-point-per-position system: 43 to win, +3 win bonus, +1 lap led, +1 most laps led.
Cup switched from carburetors to McLaren/Freescale EFI; ~$26k per car.
Dallara DW12 spec chassis at fixed $349k; 2.2L turbo V6 engines leased from Chevrolet/Honda.

Federal (SS595 205/60R13 radial) was the Legends spec tire roughly 2012-2019 (Tire Business 2010 reported ~$92/tire through distributors); Continental took over 2020; by 2024-2025 INEX rules specify USLCI-marked Hoosier tires.
GM 604 sealed crate became division-wide IMCA Modified option Jan 1 2013 - first non-claimable engine in class history; 602 crates were already allowed in SportMod and Hobby Stock.
Gen 6 car introduced; body sheet metal cost ~$15k vs $10k for CoT.
IAME X30 configuration frozen for seven years in North America (2014-2021) as SKUSA's TaG spec.
Field cap cut to 18 cars (36 pts to win), win bonus 3 (+2 if started 10th or deeper); best 18 finishes count.
UMP Pro-Mod phased to GM 602 only: non-602 engines carried 2,500 lb (2014), 2,600 (2015), 2,700 (2016) vs 2,400 for 602; open engine option re-added for 2026.
UMP Modified tire list in 2015: Hoosier A-40/A-40S/D-40/H-40/DCM 400; by 2025-26 spec moved to Hoosier M-30S with M-60 RR option.
1.170in tapered spacer cut Cup output from ~850-900 hp to ~725-750 hp (not at Daytona/Talladega).
UMP Modified shock claim $120 per shock in 2015; $350 per shock (winner only) by 2025-26.

2015 regional/national standings used best 30 of first 55 starts for Modified/Stock/Hobby/SportMod/Sport Compact; track championship bonus 1 pt per avg car count (max 20). 2026: state = first 50 events (40 for LM/Sprint/S.SportMod), bonus capped 15.

history.topic: NASCAR Super Late Model rules with CT525 (West)
history.fact: NASCAR Super Late Model rules published for 2015 (intended for 2015-2019) already listed the GM LS3 CT525 (525 hp) and SEAL sealed engines alongside 604 crates (2700 lb) and built engines (2850 lb).
DIRTcar Stock Car minimum weight 3,200 lb (2015) vs 2,800-3,000 lb by engine in 2026.
Ilmor 396 spec engine introduced in ARCA ($35k, 1,200-1,500 mi between rebuilds).
Dallara IL-15 ($234,700) + Mazda-AER 2.0 turbo, lease $88k/yr; Cooper tires 2014-2022.

IMCA license 2015: Modified $115, Late Model $135, Stock Car $95, SportMod $90, Hobby $85, Sport Compact $60; 2026: Modified $130, Late Model $115, Stock Car $110, SportMod $105, Hobby $100, Sport Compact $75.
IMCA used best 30 of first 55 starts (Mod/Stock/Hobby/SportMod/Compact) in 2015; by 2026 best 25 of first 50. LM/Sprint best 20 of first 40 both years. Track-title bonus cap fell from 20 to 15 pts.
By 2015 the NASCAR WMT spec engine (Robert Yates, aluminum block) was in use alongside built steel-block engines with a weight break; promised 30-40% savings were disputed by teams.

history.topic: Whelen Modified Tour tire price cut
history.fact: Hoosier cut WMT tire price from $190 to $150 per tire for 2015 and replaced loyalty free tires with cash contingency (~$2,500/race).
IMSA GTD BoP: e.g. BMW Z4 GT3 -50 kg (1,245 kg) and restrictor 65 -> 84 mm for 2015 Roar.
'Encumbered' finishes introduced before 2016 playoffs; 2017 L1 = 10-40 pts, L2 = 75 pts.
Charter system begins (36 charters). First sales $1.25-3.25M (MWR 2016).
F4 US launched (SCCA Pro): Honda K20 160 hp, ~$115k season; Hankook tires from 2019.
South Boston adopted a two-new-tire-per-event rule for Late Model Stocks in 2016 (Limited Sportsman one tire); moved to four new tires per event with the Hoosier ST2 in 2024, then F45* in 2025.
Tatuus USF-17 carbon chassis ($51,400) replaces spaceframe DP08.
Full USMTS-style national modified program estimated $420k from scratch (~$170k excluding $250k hauler) vs ~$250k for national DLM ops.
USPKS adopts IAME KA100 replacing Yamaha KT100 in Senior Pro.
ARCA tire supplier changes from Hoosier to General Tire (Continental bought Hoosier Oct 2016).
Stage racing: top 10 in stages 1-2 earn 10..1 points; playoff points 1 per stage win, 5 per race win.
Month of DIRTcar Summer Nationals (~29 races) cost ~$41,000: tires $14,790 (~87 @ $170), engine freshening $15,000, parts $5,000.
Cup set limits trimmed 1-3 sets at many 1.5-mile tracks (~38 sets/season saved); start race on qualifying tires.

Philip Morris 2018: 23 wins, 28 top-5s in 35 starts, 670 national pts across 5 tracks in VA/NC/SC; 5th national title (2006, 2008, 2009, 2011, 2018). Larry Phillips won 1989, 1991, 1992, 1995, 1996. Lee Pulliam 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017.

Ford Performance issued a Nov 2018 tech bulletin approving an optional COMP cam and solid roller lifters (D347SR7 'LMSC power upgrade') for Late Model Stock use, part of the built-vs-crate parity debate.
Universal aero kit replaces manufacturer kits (2 free per car, $90k each additional).
Optional Ilmor NT1 spec engine available in Truck Series to cut lease costs.
Tatuus PM-18 with 275 hp Elite-built Mazda for Pro Mazda / Indy Pro 2000.
Cup teams must run 13 sealed short blocks for two race weekends each; no engine change between Duel and Daytona 500.
550 hp high-downforce package at most ovals; 750 hp short tracks/road courses.
Michelin becomes IMSA spec tire; Continental Tire SportsCar Challenge renamed Michelin Pilot Challenge.
ARCA dropped 235-to-win/5-point-interval system for NASCAR-style 43-to-win one-point steps (max 49).
LVMS Bullring SLM allowed factory-sealed CT525 at 2700 lb (vs 2800 open, 2825 sealed SSPE/SEAL) by 2020; USA Late Model Series 2025 runs CT525 at 2900 lb with 1in restrictor.
Composite bodies mandatory at all ARCA tracks (phased from 2015).
Regional championships (4 regions) returned after being dropped post-2004; best 14 finishes; $15k to each regional champ.
Seven Indiana tracks allowed an extra right-rear (Medium or H15) per night from 2021 to curb chemical tire doping.
Hoosier sprint RR ~$200-220 in 2021, $258 in 2022 (+17%), ~$348 at 2026 retail.
WoO added ~$3,000 per standard sprint show and ~$9,000 per standard late model show in 2021 (~$1.5M added).
Due to a nationwide tire shortage IMCA allowed grooving of stamped G60 tires from June 23 2021.
Next Gen: single-source parts, 670 hp, 18in center-lock wheels, 5-speed sequential; ~$350k all-in per car.
Charter sales $6M-15M (Trackhouse $6M each from CGR; 23XI $13.5M; Spire to Kaulig $8-10M).
Div I license $225 (paper) in 2022; by 2023 $200 online / $225 at track; Charger $100/$125.

SSPE claim price rose from $21,000 (SRL 2022) to $23,000 (Montana Big 5 2025) and $26,000 + $500 (ASA southern 2025); New Smyrna suspended the claim for 2026. Part cost caps also rose (e.g. crank $2200 -> $2400, rods $1600 -> $1800).
From March 10 2023 WoO sprint rears must be Hoosier: RR D15A/Medium, LR D12A.
WoO Sprint points fund $1.025M in 2023; champion could earn $350k with exclusivity bonus (same $350k paid 2024).
Indy Lights rebranded Indy NXT; Firestone replaces Cooper.

LMSC tracks balance GM 604 crates, Ford D347SR, Harrington Enforcer and built 'upgrade' engines with weight; e.g. Florence gave the 604 a 50 lb break vs the Ford 347SR, while CARS Tour 2025 put the GM 'Upgrade' at 3150 lb vs 3100 for others.
Connor Hall Div I champion 2024: 592 pts, 18 wins in 26 starts, 24 top-5s; runner-ups Burt Myers 522, Jacob Goede 520.
USF Pro Championships switch from Cooper to Continental (built by Hoosier), five-year deal.
Snowball Derby SLMs ran Hoosier ST1 lefts / ST3 rights in 2024 and switched to Hoosier F-45* all around for 2025.
Standard WoO Sprint show purse raised from about $58k to $70k; $12k to win.
F4 US switches to Ligier JS F422 ($114,800 vs ~$65k), grid shrinks.
SKUSA spec tire is Evinco (SK-M2 red / SK-H2 blue); MG remains rain tire.
IndyCar hybrid ERS (supercapacitor, ~60 hp) debuts mid-2024.
Live Fast charter sold to Spire for $40M (record).
IMCA Modified claim is $1,050 cash or $100 + exchange (2024 and 2026 rulebooks); exact year raised from ~$550 not confirmed.

2024 IMCA national champions: Modified Chaz Baca (28 wins), Stock Car Mike Nichols (30 wins, 13th title), Late Model Cory Dumpert (15 wins, 6th straight), Northern SportMod Matthew Looft (33 wins), Hobby Stock Cory Probst (29 wins).
Champion award $200k (2024) -> $250k (2025); fund paid top 12 (2024, ~$935k listed) -> top 15 (2025, $1.59M listed).
DIRTcar UMP Modifieds allow the 'DC18' sealed Chevrolet CT525 aluminum crate (non-claimable) alongside open claim engines (2025 rules).
Short Track Super Series (12th season in 2025) unified Modified engine/weight rules into three weights and uses American Racer exclusively.
Wiscasset Speedway added a 2025 rebuild-and-reseal option for 602 crates citing limited availability and high cost of new 602 engines; ACT by contrast barred rebuilding/refreshing 602 LMS motors.
INEX 2025 rulebook allows the newer Yamaha FZ09/MT09 engine (1230 lb min with asphalt tires) alongside the traditional Yamaha FJ1200/XJR1200/XJR1250 (1280 lb).
POWRi 305 sprints adopted IMCA RaceSaver rules in 2025.

Stewart-Haas charters sold for $26.5M-29.5M each ($84M total).
ASCS National Tour min weight raised from 1,475 to 1,500 lb for 2025.
World 100 to-win hit $100k in 2026 after $72k (2025) and decades of +$1k/yr.
New Smyrna's 2026 SLM rules temporarily suspended the SSPE claim option due to lack of engine availability and extended build times.

history.fact: USA Late Model Series allowed Brodix dry-sump/aluminum-head engines with 0.95in restrictor in 2025 only; all dry-sump engines phased out for 2026, leaving crate/wet-sump packages.
IMCA Modified license $115 (2015) -> $130 (2026); Hobby Stock $85 -> $100; Sport Compact $60 -> $75; Late Model $135 -> $115 (dropped).
Win worth 55 points; playoff points dropped; 10-race, 16-driver Chase with seeded points (2,100 down to 2,000) and no eliminations.
Hoosier was exclusive WMT tire supplier 1999-2025; American Racer became official supplier from the 2026 season (tests Nov-Dec 2025).
Cup output raised from 670 to 750 hp at tracks under 1.5 miles (announced Oct 2025).
